title: Elapsed Time on a Number Line

steps.body: How long is it from 8:40 to 9:20? Lay time on a number line and **JUMP**: a friendly hop to 9:00 (20 minutes), then a hop to 9:20 (20 more). Two hops, 40 minutes. The hour border is your stepping stone — always land on it first.

widget.prompt: Build the jump plan for the gap from 2:45 to 3:25.

commonBuilds.feedback: The hops say 15 + 25 = 40. A 70 could only come from adding the clock labels (45 + 25) — but jumps measure the GAP between times, not the labels on them.

widget.missFeedback: Hop to the hour first (2:45 → 3:00 costs 15), then hop to the target (25 more) — the gap is the two hops added.
widget.successFeedback: 15 + 25 = 40 minutes — the hour border crossed in two friendly hops.

explanationVariants: Hop to the hour: 9:45 → 10:00 is 15; then 10:00 → 10:20 is 20 more. Total 35 minutes.
Count up by fives past the border: 9:50, 9:55, 10:00 (15)… then 20 straight to 10:20.

widget.prompt: Recess runs from 9:45 to 10:20. How many minutes is that?

commonErrors.feedback: 65 added the minute labels (45 + 20). Labels aren't lengths — jump the border instead: 15 to the hour, 20 past it.
25 subtracted 20 from 45 — backwards across the hour! Time only runs forward: 9:45 → 10:00 → 10:20.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Two hops: 9:45 to 10:00, then 10:00 to 10:20 — add them.

steps.body: Why not just subtract the minute labels? Because **the hour rolls over at 60** — there is no 9:75 hiding after 9:59. Crossing an hour, label arithmetic breaks; the two-hop jump never does. That's the whole trick.

explanationVariants: Split the 35 at the border: 20 minutes reach 6:00, and the other 15 land at 6:15.
5:40 plus 35 can't be 5:75 — sixty minutes fills the hour and the count restarts at 6:00.

widget.prompt: A movie starts at 5:40 and runs 35 minutes. Set the clock to show when it ends.
widget.successFeedback: 20 minutes to reach 6:00, then 15 more — the border split makes it easy.
widget.minuteFeedback: That added a whole extra chunk — 5:40 + 35 splits as 20-to-the-hour + 15 past it: 6:15.
widget.hourFeedback: 5:15 is BEFORE the movie starts. Adding time moves forward: past 6:00 to 6:15.

cml.actionGoal: Coordinate hour and minute positions while composing elapsed time on a 60-minute cycle.

widget.prompt: The timeline starts at 1:50. Slide to the total minutes that reach 2:30.
widget.lowFeedback: Not far enough — you haven't reached 2:30 yet. (Hint: 10 minutes only reaches 2:00.)
widget.highFeedback: Too far — you've jumped past 2:30. Ease back.
widget.successFeedback: 40 minutes: 10 to land on 2:00, then 30 more to 2:30. The border hop plus the leftover.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents elapsed time.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for elapsed time must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines elapsed time.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

predict.reveal: 40 minutes: 10 to reach 2:00, then 30 more. Subtracting the minute labels gives 30 − 50 = −20, which is nonsense — the hour rolls over at 60, not at 100. Hopping to the whole hour first keeps you clear of that trap entirely.

explanationVariants: Land on 7:00 first (25 minutes), then hop the remaining 10 — totals 35 with zero rollover risk.
The hour border is the friendly number of time arithmetic — jumps through it never break.

widget.prompt: What's the fastest RELIABLE way to count the minutes from 6:35 to 7:10?

options.label: Hop to 7:00 (that's 25 minutes), then 10 more — total 35
options.feedback: Two friendly hops through the border — quick, and immune to rollover mistakes.

options.label: Compute 35 − 10 = 25
options.feedback: That subtracts minute labels across an hour border — it misses the hour's structure entirely. The real gap is 35.

options.label: Count every single minute, one by one
options.feedback: It works — thirty-five careful counts — but the border hop gets the same 35 in two moves. Save the counting for checking.

options.label: Compute 70 − 35
options.feedback: Where would a 70 come from? Clock minutes never pass 59 — cross the hour by hopping, not by inventing minutes.

hints: One task at a time — where does the clock stand after reading?
From 4:55: hop 5 minutes to 5:00, then the rest.
explanationVariants: Reading: 4:35 + 20 = 4:55. Math: 4:55 + 25 splits at the border — 5 to reach 5:00, 20 more — landing at 5:20.
Total work is 45 minutes from 4:35: 25 to reach 5:00, then 20 past it. Same 5:20 either way.

widget.prompt: Maya starts homework at 4:35. Reading takes 20 minutes, then math takes 25 more. Set the clock to show when she is done.
widget.successFeedback: 4:35 → 4:55 after reading; then 5 minutes to the border and 20 past it — 5:20.
widget.minuteFeedback: 5:00 is mid-math — reading ended at 4:55 and only 5 of math's 25 minutes fit before the border. Twenty more follow: 5:20.
widget.hourFeedback: 4:55 is when READING ends — the math session hasn't happened yet. Add its 25 minutes across the border.

cml.actionGoal: Coordinate hour and minute positions while composing elapsed time on a 60-minute cycle.

steps.body: You can measure any gap now.
takeaways: Elapsed time = jumps on a timeline; land on the hour border first.
Never add or subtract minute labels across an hour — there is no :75.
Multi-task stories chain the hops: finish one task's clock before starting the next.
steps.teaser: next chapter: leaving the clock for the scale — grams, kilograms, and what 'heavy' really means.

concept.body: Quick rewind. The hour border is a **stepping stone in the stream** — always land on :00 first. From 2:50, don't leap straight for 3:10: step to 3:00 (10 minutes), then step to 3:10 (10 more). Two small dry steps beat one wet leap.

explanationVariants: Step to 3:00 (10 minutes), then to 3:10 (10 more): 20 in all.
Two ten-minute steps across the border.

options.feedback: Ten to the border, ten past it.
60 added the labels (50 + 10). The stepping-stone route counts the real gap: 10 + 10 = 20.
40 subtracted the labels (50 − 10) — backwards across the border. Step forward instead: 10 + 10.
